subject: Hosted API security assessment — report request & encrypted transfer proposal
messages:
From: Sabrina Lowe <sabrina.lowe@healthquest.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 12 Nov 2025 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Request — latest penetration test for Hosted API and secure transfer options

Hi Kimberly,

We're preparing a security review for our platform team and need the latest penetration test report for Redwood's Hosted API (full report, not just the exec summary). Our compliance reviewers will also want the report dates, testing scope, and the name of the external vendor that performed the assessment.

Can you share the report and let us know what secure transfer options you support? We prefer a method that avoids email attachments for the full PDF (S3 presigned link, secure portal, or an encrypted archive). Also, we have to cross-check against our SIG/CAIQ questionnaire — if you can indicate the redaction policy (client names/identifiers), that helps.

I can loop in our security contact (Jordan Park) if you need to coordinate an out-of-band decryption key or phone verification.

Thanks,
Sabrina Lowe
Security Program Manager, HealthQuest
Sabrina.Lowe@healthquest.com

---
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Sabrina Lowe <sabrina.lowe@healthquest.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 12 Nov 2025 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request — latest penetration test for Hosted API and secure transfer options

Hi Sabrina — thanks for the note.

We can absolutely provide the penetration test artifacts and a scope attestation. A couple quick clarifying questions so we send the right package:
- Do you need the full, unredacted report (including any customer identifiers) or is an anonymized version acceptable?
- Does your reviewer need evidence of remediation (i.e., a short status matrix) or just the raw report and dates?

Secure transfer options we support:
- Time-limited, encrypted S3 presigned URL (recommended; configurable expiry)
- One-time encrypted zip (AES-256) we send via S3 + phone-delivered passphrase to your security contact
- Access to our Secure Review portal (ephemeral viewer session NDA required; good for in-person risk reviews)
- On a case-by-case basis we can provide an encrypted SFTP drop with short-lived credentials.

I'm attaching a one-page executive summary to unblock your reviewers while we coordinate delivery of the full report. If you can confirm whether anonymization is required and the preferred transfer method (S3 presigned preferred), we'll proceed.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Account Executive — Strategic Health
Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood-pt-exec-summary-2025.pdf

---
From: Sabrina Lowe <sabrina.lowe@healthquest.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Park <jordan.park@healthquest.com>
Date: Thu, 13 Nov 2025 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request — latest penetration test for Hosted API and secure transfer options

Thanks, Kimberly — attaching Jordan for coordination.

Our reviewers need the full report (redaction of third-party customer identifiers is acceptable). We also need the testing window (dates) and the external vendor name. For transfer, we prefer a presigned S3 URL with at least 7 days of access so our team can download and review; if that's not feasible, a 72-hour link would be our minimum.

Jordan: can you confirm a mobile number we can use for one-time passphrases if needed?

Appreciate the exec summary — that'll help while you arrange the rest.

Sabrina

---
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Sabrina Lowe <sabrina.lowe@healthquest.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 13 Nov 2025 10:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request — latest penetration test for Hosted API and secure transfer options

Hi Sabrina / Kimberly,

I can take point on the secure delivery. Proposed approach (we've used this with other healthcare customers):
1) Prepare an encrypted archive of the full penetration test PDF + scope attestation + remediation matrix. We will redact non-Redwood customer identifiers per your request.
2) Upload the encrypted archive to an S3 bucket and provide a presigned URL with a 72-hour expiry. If HealthQuest needs 7 days, we can accommodate for this customer — please confirm.
3) Deliver the decryption passphrase out-of-band. We will deliver the passphrase only to a designated security contact (Jordan Park) via SMS or phone call after identity confirmation.
4) Include a short vendor attestation: vendor name (Silverline Security LLC), testing window (2025-09-08 to 2025-09-12), and a summary of the scope (Hosted API endpoints + authentication flows + admin console surface).

Attachments: redwood-sharing-playbook.pdf (internal playbook that outlines our evidence transfer checklist and redaction policy).

If you prefer a longer review window or need an in-session walkthrough with our security engineering team, we can schedule a Secure Review portal session (NDA first). Let us know Jordan's preferred contact method and whether 72 hours is acceptable.

Regards,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Security Operations, Redwood Inference

---
From: Sabrina Lowe <sabrina.lowe@healthquest.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 14 Nov 2025 09:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request — latest penetration test for Hosted API and secure transfer options

Vivek — that plan works for us. Confirming: 72 hours is acceptable; we would prefer 7 days but can make 72 work if the vendor constraints require it. Please include the vendor attestation and testing window in the package.

Jordan's mobile for out-of-band passphrase: +1 (415) 555-0182. You can call or SMS to confirm identity.

Also: can you confirm whether the report includes any HIPAA-related findings or if Redwood treats HIPAA control evidence separately? Our compliance team flagged that as a possible item to check.

If you can share the presigned link and expected time of availability, we'll expedite the downloads on our side. Thanks for moving quickly on this.

—Sabrina
Security Program Manager, HealthQuest
